season.short_description: Season of the cumulative estimate, written as 2025-26.
season.long_description: Season the cumulative estimate belongs to.

vaccine.short_description: Flu (seasonal influenza vaccine, 2019-20 onward) or rsv (maternal RSV vaccine, 2025-26).
vaccine.long_description: Vaccine the estimate refers to. For flu, seasonal influenza vaccine received before or during pregnancy since July 1 of the season. For rsv, RSV vaccine (Abrysvo) received during pregnancy, recommended at 32-36 weeks' gestation during September through January.

race_ethnicity.short_description: Race and ethnicity of the pregnant women, using CDC's labels.
race_ethnicity.long_description: Race and ethnicity group as labelled by CDC. NH stands for non-Hispanic. Overall includes women with unknown race and ethnicity.

vsd_coverage.long_name: Cumulative percent of pregnant women 18-49 vaccinated
vsd_coverage.short_description: Percent of pregnant women ages 18-49 who had received the vaccine as of the week ending date.
vsd_coverage.long_description: Cumulative percent of women ages 18-49 with a pregnancy during the season who had received the vaccine, from electronic health records in the Vaccine Safety Datalink. For flu, the denominator is women pregnant during August through March and the numerator counts vaccines received since July 1. For RSV, the denominator is women who reached 32 weeks' gestation since September 1. Coverage can fall from one week to the next as newly identified pregnancies are added.
vsd_coverage.statement: {value}% of pregnant women in VSD health systems had received the vaccine as of {time}

vsd_denominator.long_name: Number of pregnant women in the coverage denominator

vsd.name: Vaccine Safety Datalink (VSD) pregnancy vaccination coverage
vsd.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
vsd.location: Percent of Pregnant Women Ages 18-49 Years Who Have Received an Influenza (or RSV) Vaccine, by Race and Ethnicity (FluVaxView and RSVVaxView dashboards)
vsd.description: The Vaccine Safety Datalink (VSD) is a collaboration between CDC's Immunization Safety Office and integrated health care organizations that uses electronic health records to monitor vaccine safety. CDC uses the VSD to publish weekly cumulative flu vaccination coverage among pregnant women ages 18-49 from the 2019-20 season, and RSV vaccination coverage among pregnant women who reach 32 weeks' gestation, overall and by race and ethnicity. The current data come from 10 reporting sites. Estimates are national only, describe VSD members rather than all pregnant women, can change as pregnancies are identified, and may miss vaccines given outside the health system.
vsd.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.
